The PCA pump shall perform a power-on self-test 142 (POST) to assure system integrity after being turned on, yet before any infusion begins. Failure of POST shall raise a POST alarm , stop pump, record it in the Fault Log, and display the reason for failure on the user interface. (EC4 §4.2.4)

The PCA pump shall perform periodic self-tests 143 to assure system integrity during long periods of use. Failure of a self-test shall raise a self-test alarm , stop pump, record it in the Fault Log, and display the reason for failure on the user interface. (EC22c §4.2.22)
The PCA pump shall have continuous fault-detection144 and masking. Hardware monitors of thread heartbeat, memory error correction codes are examples. (EC22d §4.2.22)
Occurrence of unavoidable single-event upsets 145 caused by cosmic-ray-induced high- and thermalenergy neutrons must be either masked, or detected to fail-stop. (EC22d §4.2.22)

Each log entry shall have a time stamp 88 with its time of occurrence.

Successfully masked faults 146 shall be recorded in the Fault Log, but not raise an alarm. (EC22e §4.2.22)
All unmasked hardware detected faults147 shall raise a fault alarm, stop pump, record it in the Fault Log, and display the reason for fault on the user interface. (EC22 §4.2.22)
The fault log shall record at least 1000 faults before overwriting oldest fault records first. 92
A real-time clock93 must produce timestamps accurate to 10 ms.
